companyDescription: Memory · DRAM + NAND + HBM for AI accelerators · HBM sold out for 2026 · FQ4 FY26 revenue $54.2B, FQ1 FY27 guide $61.5B ± $1.5B (vs ~$57B Street)
priceNote: Live $707.70 (+19.0%, Nov 23 close, Yahoo) on the NVIDIA/Huang relief rally. About 42% below the $1,213.56 52-week high and below both the 50-day (~$908) and the 200-day (~$774). It fell 17.5% on Nov 5 alone in the AI/chip selloff.
summary: The AI memory leader has de-rated about 42% from its high while guidance keeps rising. FQ4 revenue was $54.2B and the FQ1 guide is $61.5B ± $1.5B, against a ~$57B Street estimate going in. HBM is sold out for 2026. The FQ1 report is confirmed for Dec 17 (company release, Nov 19). Consensus sits around $1,560 (+120%) with 45 Buy/Strong Buy ratings, but the dispersion is huge ($361–$2,500). The catalyst is 23 days out, beyond the 14d North Star window. Base +15% assumes a clean beat-and-raise into January, a 4–6 week horizon above the core P75 (10.8%).

catalysts.name: FQ1 FY27 earnings (Dec 17)
catalysts.description: Confirmed by Micron's Nov 19 release: call Dec 17, 2026 at 2:30pm MT. Guide was $61.5B ± $1.5B. The read is HBM pricing for 2027 and whether capex discipline holds.

catalysts.name: FOMC Dec 9 + CPI Dec 10
catalysts.description: Macro stack one week before the print: a +25bp hike is ~91% priced; a 50bp surprise would hit high-beta semis first.

risks: Memory is cyclical: 66% gross margins in the cloud memory unit invite new supply that eventually pushes prices down.
Extreme volatility: -17.5% on Nov 5 and +19% on Nov 23; a beat can still sell off if 2027 HBM pricing disappoints.
Policy: the Nov 5 drop was tied to midterm results that could curb data-center construction.
Macro WAIT (15/100) with FOMC/CPI one week before the print.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds 3.75–4.00%. CME FedWatch prices a +25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC at ~91% (Nov 23); futures dropped the 50bp tail after the November selloff.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Oct core CPI +0.3% m/m (hot). Sep core PCE 3.1% y/y; Oct PCE (Nov 25) consensus 3.2% is the last inflation print before the Fed.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Semis are high-beta to rates and AI-capex sentiment; MU's earnings momentum gives it more support than pre-profit AI names.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — /macro is WAIT (15/100, high conviction): S&P 7,237 is still below its 200-day (~7,340) after the Nov 23 +4.7% squeeze, VIX 27, breadth ~43% above 50DMA, HY OAS widening to ~3.52%. Core prior is largely unmeasured in this regime (8/174 windows had SPY down >2%).
